column1: # `zig build check-portable`'s known-failure baseline, keyed by (module, target)
# — see build.zig's check-portable comment and CONVENTIONS.md §4 for the full
# schema (`meta.targets`: `.linux64` / `.linux32` / `.windows` / `.wasm32`).
# One row per (module, target) pair the module DECLARES in `meta.targets`
# whose test binary currently fails to COMPILE for that target. `.linux64` is
# never cross-compiled by this gate (proven by the default test suite
# instead) and can never appear here.
# Format: <module><TAB><target><TAB><reason>, one line per pair. `#`-comment
# and blank lines are ignored. The reason is copied from the actual `zig
# build portable-<module>-<target>` compiler error -- never invented, never a
# generic restatement that could be pasted onto any row. Local toolchain
# install paths are stripped down to the `std/...`-relative path (no
# `/home/<user>/` in this file, ever — CLAUDE.md).
# THIS LIST IS A BASELINE, NOT A SUPPRESSION. `check-portable`
# (`PortableBaselineStep` in build.zig) fails the build in BOTH directions:
#   - a (module, target) pair NOT listed here that fails to compile -- a new
#     or previously-undetected regression;
#   - a pair LISTED here that now PASSES -- a stale entry, which must be
#     deleted, not left for "in case it comes back". A baseline that can only
#     grow is a list nobody re-reads, which is exactly the shape this repo has
#     been burned by before (`check-global-alloc`'s `global-alloc-ok:` markers
#     enforce the identical rule for the identical reason).
# Fixing a declared target's compile does not require asking permission to
# shrink this file -- the gate REQUIRES the row gone the moment it passes.
# ── 2026-08-18: SCHEMA CHANGE, how this file's contents were decided ──
# Before this date, `check-portable` swept every `platform = .any` module for
# wasm32 regardless of whether the module ever intended wasm32 — 64 of them
# were listed here as "known failures", most of them FALSE ALARMS in the sense
# that mattered: `http`, `aaa-gate`, `ratelimit`, `bbs` and the rest never
# meant to target wasm32 at all. `meta.targets` fixes the conflation between
# "author intends cross-platform" and "someone verified a target" -- but the
# fix is NOT "only declare a target a module's own docs happen to mention".
# The first pass at this schema tried that and it was wrong: it shrank 195
# swept modules down to 5, which would have permanently blinded the gate to
# whatever it had not already been told to look for -- exactly backwards for a
# gate whose entire job is catching what nobody declared a claim about yet.
# The corrected rule: a REAL CONSUMER that cross-compiles a module for a
# target is what earns that module the declaration -- stronger evidence than
# any doc sentence, because it is a build that either works or does not.
# Read directly from the consuming repos' own build.zig graphs (2026-08-18):
#   - `~/workspace/axp/axp-core/build.zig` imports 30 zig-libs modules; AXP's
#     device agent cross-compiles to static musl on big-endian MIPS32
#     (`~/workspace/axp/docs/feasibility-mips.md`). Of those 30, 9 are
#     explicitly commented "Host-side only ... NOT in the device agent's
#     dependency graph" (the REST cluster `http`/`router`/`aaa-gate`/`cors`/
#     `staticfiles`/`accesslog`/`validate`/`security-headers`) plus `mcp`
#     (axp-mcp is a facade over axp-central's store, confirmed host-side by
#     its own build.zig doc comment, not part of the device agent either).
#     The other 21 gained `.linux32`: `sealedbox`, `hashdigest`, `framing`,
#     `tar`, `icmp`, `dns`, `filestore`, `blobmsg`, `blobstore`, `l2disco`,
#     `rawsock`, `uci`, `traceroute`, `probe`, `stun`, `sntp`, `procnet`,
#     `netlink`, `conntrack`, `nl80211`, `wireguard`. Only modules AXP's own
#     build.zig explicitly labels host-side were excluded; everything else
#     compiles into the device agent's binary and was declared, per the
#     asymmetry that over-declaring costs only CI time while under-declaring
#     silently deletes coverage.
#   - `~/workspace/bxp/bxp-core/build.zig` imports 12 zig-libs modules, and
#     CI (`~/workspace/bxp/.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs the whole test
#     matrix including `windows-latest`; `bxp-gui-bridge` ships as
#     `bxp-gui-bridge.dll` on Windows (`bxp-gui-bridge/build.zig`) and spawns
#     `bxp-cli.exe` as a child on the same platform
#     (`docs/dev/architecture/gui.md`, the `TerminateProcess` reap path). All
#     12 gained `.windows`: `json5`, `diagnostics`, `decimal`, `numparse`,
#     `minisign`, `procrun`, `mcp`, `encoding`, `csvstream`, `zipstream`,
#     `tz`, `datefmt`.
# `.linux32`'s real cross-compile query is `mips-linux-musl` +
# `mips32,soft_float` (AXP's own probe query, ath79 24Kc has no FPU) --
# corrected from an earlier `musleabihf` guess, which would have silently
# picked a hard-float ABI AXP's hardware cannot run. `.windows` is unchanged,
# `x86_64-windows-gnu`.
# Kept from before the consumer read: `qr`/`qrscan` declare `.wasm32` (the
# task's own static-footprint use case, both pass); `reconcilable` declares
# `.windows` + `.wasm32` (its own SPEC/README already say "verified by
# compiling ... not just claimed" -- a self-reported build, not bare prose,
# both pass); `procrun` and `diskusage`'s SPEC-based declarations turned out
# to be independently corroborated by the consumer read above (`procrun` is
# literally one of bxp's 12; `diskusage` is not imported by either consumer,
# so its `.linux32` claim rests on its own SPEC's "builds and analyzes
# cleanly" account, not a live import -- kept, but weaker evidence than the
# rest of this file and flagged here as such). All pass.
# Result: 38 (module, target) pairs declared, 34 pass, 4 real failures below
# -- this is the honest shape of a non-empty baseline, not a regression.
# ── Root-cause groups (2026-08-18, mips-linux-musl mips32/soft_float) ──
#   64-bit atomic RMW unsupported at the mips32 baseline ISA (own bug):
#     blobstore, filestore -- same class independently confirmed on `ramcache`
#     below, which does not declare `.linux32` and so has no row of its own.
#   usize-narrow (u64 -> usize), own bug:
#     traceroute
#   deliberate big-endian guard (module says so itself, not a surprise):
#     wireguard -- `handshake.zig`'s `comptime` block already `@compileError`s
#     with an explanation and a fix recipe; a second, independent u64->usize
#     narrow in `transport.zig` also fires (11 errors total, same build).
# module
wireguard
column3: modules/wireguard/src/handshake.zig:57: the module's own deliberate @compileError guard. DECISION, NOT DEBT: keep it. createInitiation/createResponse assign msg.type/sender_index/receiver_index (the only multi-byte ints in the wire structs) natively and MAC over asBytes(&msg), so a big-endian host produces a self-consistent but non-interoperable handshake -- worse than a build failure. The guard's fix recipe is mechanically right but understates scope: 28 asBytes/memcpy sites treat struct layout as wire bytes (6 production, ~20 in the byte-exact KATs that anchor this module) and no production bytes->struct parser exists yet, so real support is a wire-boundary rewrite of the crypto data plane. Measured: a control-plane-only consumer (open/setDevice/keyFromBase64/AllowedIp.parse) cross-compiles clean for mips-linux-musl and never trips the guard -- Zig analyses handshake.zig only on an actual reference, which this module's own test forces and a consumer does not. AXP ships exactly that path; on OpenWRT the data plane is the kernel's. Revisit only if someone ships the userspace data plane big-endian.
